3.0.0.en: When the affliction on Tobit increased, he did not sin against God or against men, but expressed his feelings and cast all his burden upon God, in a prayer full of feelings of sorrow and groaning from the affliction, and he mingled his prayer with his tears. It was a prayer from the heart. And he offered a complete prayer that included:

3.1.0.en: 1- Glorifying God, for he ascribed to Him justice, uprightness, mercy, truth and wisdom.

3.2.0.en: A byword: he became a subject of men's mockery and talk.

3.2.1.en: 2- Confession in repentance of sin, not only his own sins, but the sins of his fathers, their failure to keep the commandments of God, the impure heart and the unclean intention. These sins led to their falling into captivity and their being exposed to plunder and killing; indeed they became a reproach and a worthless people, despised.

3.3.0.en: 3- Under the pressure of the affliction upon him, he asked that God would permit and command that his life be ended, that he might be delivered from these troubles. But he set a condition for his request, that it be according to the will of God. Here trust in God and submission to Him appear.

3.4.s.en: (2) Sara the daughter of Raguel and the death of her seven husbands

3.4.0.en: Sara: a Hebrew word meaning princess.

3.4.1.en: Raguel: a Hebrew word meaning friend of God.

3.4.2.en: This family was bound to God in love and friendship, as appears from this book. Sara was distinguished in her relationship with God, as a princess. She lived in a small city near the city of Rages in the land of the Medes, which the Assyrians had taken, and to which they had transferred some Jews, as we mentioned earlier. Because the city of Raguel was near Rages, it was called by its name, Rages being taken to include the great city and the surrounding country. On the very day when Tobit heard a reproach from his wife Anna, Sara heard a reproach from one of her father's maidservants. This shows that Raguel was a rich man, with a large house and maidservants.

3.5.0.en: Asmodeus: the name of a Persian pagan god. The name Asmodeus means the spirit of violence and destruction, or the spirit of sexual lust.

3.5.1.en: The reason for the maidservant's reproach of her mistress was that Sara had been married, and on the wedding night, as soon as her husband entered the chamber to be united with her, a demon named Asmodeus attacked him. (All the gods of the Gentiles are demons.) He represents cruelty, violence, and the killing of the husband. This happened seven times, that is, the devil killed seven husbands who tried to be united with Sara. Perhaps they were from the Gentiles. The number seven represents completeness, which shows the authority of the devil. Perhaps Sara's husbands were not of the people of God, that is, they were pagans, unbelievers, or Jews who did not hold fast to the faith and the commandments of God. Whoever they were, the reason for their union with her was bodily lust and the wealth that she enjoyed.

3.6.0.en: When one of the maidservants erred in some task, her mistress Sara rebuked her, and the maidservant answered her insolently, with false accusations, and reproached her that she had failed in marriage seven times and therefore had borne neither a son nor a daughter like other women. She also falsely accused her of being the killer of the seven husbands, a thing that even ordinary logic rejects: why would a bride kill the bridegroom with whom she rejoiced to be united?

3.7.0.en: The maidservant also accused her mistress of attempting to kill her, by asking: Do you want to kill me?

3.8.0.en: Because the reproach was severe, Sara was greatly distressed and went up to a room on the upper floor (an upper chamber) and stayed in it three days and three nights, tasting no food, in continual fasting and prayer with tears, that God might take away her reproach.

3.8.1.en: In ancient times the devout Jews would sometimes build on the roofs of their houses a small room, in which they spent some time in worship and prayer. They made windows for this room facing the direction of the temple in Jerusalem, even in the days of the captivity, that they might remember the temple of God and offer worship to Him. This upper room is mentioned in the life of Daniel (Dan 6:10, 11) and also in the life of Judith (Jdt 9:1). We also note the upper room of the house of St. Mark, in which Christ gathered with His disciples and instituted the sacrament of the Eucharist, and in which He also appeared after His resurrection and the Holy Spirit came upon them (Mk 14:15, Acts 1:13). Tears show the intensity of her sorrow. Tears are repeated often in this book, which shows the tenderness of feeling and the strength of emotion in the characters who appear in it, whether in sorrow or in joy. These are the occasions on which tears are mentioned in this book:-

3.8.2.en: 1- Tobit's weeping at the feast when he rose to bury one of the dead Jews (ch. 2:7).

3.8.3.en: 2- Tobit's tears in his prayer, after he lost his sight (ch. 3:1).

3.8.4.en: 3- Sara's weeping, after her maidservant's reproach of her (ch. 3:10).

3.8.5.en: 4- The weeping of Tobias's mother over him, after his parting from her and his journey to recover the value of the bond (ch. 5:18).

3.8.6.en: 5- The weeping of Raguel and his wife Anna and their daughter Sara, when they met and came to know the younger Tobias (ch. 7:6-8).

3.8.7.en: 6- The weeping of Anna, Sara's mother, at the marriage of her daughter, for fear of Tobias's death (ch. 7:16).

3.8.8.en: 7- The weeping of Gabael on meeting Tobias in the house of Raguel, rejoicing at meeting him (ch. 9:6).

3.8.9.en: 8- The weeping of Anna, Tobias's mother, because of Tobias's delay in returning from his journey (ch. 10:3, 7).

3.8.10.en: 9- The weeping of Tobit and Anna his wife at the return of their son Tobias (ch. 11:9, 13).

3.9.0.en: It was a prayer without murmuring, for Sara blessed God in it.

3.9.1.en: God is a refuge for His children who believe in Him. When Anna reproached Tobit her husband, he hurried to prayer and did not quarrel with his wife, nor did he take refuge in human beings who were unable to help him. So also Sara hurried to be alone with God in fasting and prayer, in the face of her maidservant's reproaches and accusations. God is our heavenly Father, and His door is always open to us with love and tenderness, to hear our prayers and help us in our afflictions, and even to remove them from us and give us comfort and peace during the affliction and all the days of our life. May we hurry to God like these two saints, Tobit and Sara, and find our rest in the Church and her sacraments, that is, in confession, Communion and all the means of grace, especially prayer and the Holy Bible.

3.10.0.en: 1- Her humility and her confession of her sin, and also her hope in the merciful God, who, though He permits some affliction, returns to have mercy and lift the trial.

3.11.0.en: 3- Her asking God to take away the shame that wearies her in soul and humiliates her, or to end her life on earth according to His will. This shows the degree of distress she was suffering.

3.12.0.en: Then the devout Sara declares here her holding fast to a life of chastity, as a maiden before marriage.

3.13.0.en: And likewise her withdrawal from reckless young men who love corrupt worldly amusements.

3.14.0.en: Also, when she accepted marriage her aim was not bodily lust but the forming of a family in the fear of God. Because of the purity of her heart, the devil Asmodeus was not able to touch her with harm while he killed her husbands, and this confirms that they came to marriage only for the purpose of bodily lust.

3.15.0.en: In humility and submission to the will of God, she accepted the failure of her seven previous marriages, for she believes that they were not suitable for her, and in humility she says that she was not worthy of them. And in hope she awaits the man whom God prepares as a suitable husband for her.

3.16.0.en: Finally Sara declares her faith in the loftiness of God's wisdom.

3.17.0.en: And although God permits chastening, all His children trust that He returns to rescue them and have mercy on them. For God desires and rejoices in the salvation of His children and not their destruction, and is pleased with their joy and rejoicing, so He permits the affliction in order to give them joy afterward.

3.18.0.en: He deserves blessing and honor forever. Thus Sara ends her prayer with the glorification of God and submission to Him.

3.18.1.en: Sara is an example for the balanced young person, who cares for a life of purity in all his conduct and speech, even if he sacrifices some impure friends, however dear they are, and even if he sacrifices some amusements and gatherings that make a person lose his purity. My young brethren, and every person, are you careful in your life to keep purity and to enjoy fellowship with God and His love?

3.18.2.en: And do the young people who are approaching marriage follow the thinking and conduct of Sara? Let the basis of choice not be built on outward beauty, desires and material things, but let it be the choice of the person who works to form a Christian family and develops the relationship with God, so that we may enjoy feelings of pure love in intimacy and affection in union with Christ Jesus.

3.19.s.en: (4) The answering of the prayers of Tobit and Sara

3.19.0.en: Here fervent prayers appear, springing from the heart, which the angels immediately lift up before the throne of the great God in heaven, and we see how God answers these prayers with concern, for He sent the great archangel Raphael to resolve the affliction of each of them and heal him of his troubles.

3.20.0.en: Raphael: one of the three great archangels, Michael, Gabriel and Raphael. The meaning of his name is the compassion of God.

3.20.1.en: This shows not only God's love and tenderness toward us, but also the love of the angels and their service to us. The Church celebrates the angel Raphael on the third day of the Little Month (Nasie). St. John Chrysostom says that on this day the angel Raphael appeared to the disciples of Christ. There is another feast of the angel Raphael, in remembrance of the building of the first church in his name, which was built by King Arcadius on the shore of the Bosphorus; this feast falls on the 13th of Koiak.

4.0.1.en: After Tobit prayed, his heart was at ease, and he felt that God would answer him and deliver him from his affliction. This shows his strong faith, but he imagined, or supposed, that his deliverance from the affliction would be by the ending of his life. (God did indeed answer, but He appointed another solution to his affliction, by healing him of his illness, as will appear later.)

4.0.2.en: How happy is the person who believes that God answers his prayer, for his heart is at rest and is assured that he has cast his problem, indeed his whole life, into the faithful hand that cares for him and loves him more than he loves himself, namely the tender hand of God. And in proportion as he directs his heart in prayer toward God in all his needs, he feels a peace that surpasses all understanding and enjoys a constant joy.

4.1.0.en: Therefore Tobit called his son to give him his last charge, which was very precious counsel that every person needs, for it represents the essence of the thought of St. Tobit, who asked his son to make it the foundation of his life.

4.2.0.en: The faith of Tobit the father was that it is God who will take his spirit at death, and this is the faith of all the children of God. He then charged his son to bury his body.

4.3.0.en: Then he charged him to honor his mother, reminding him of what she had endured for him in conceiving and giving birth and in all her care of him. This is what every person ought to remember, remembering all that his parents endured for him, so that he hurries to honor them, carrying out the commandment of God, and continues so all the days of their lives, and after this buries them with honor.

4.4.0.en: The father charged that his wife's body be buried beside his own, and this shows his love for her, even after death, forgetting her anger and her reproach of him and all her faults. For love forgets offense and forgives.

4.4.1.en: My brother, may you forgive others their faults quickly, so that your heart may be cleansed and love may be the ruling power in your feelings toward them, and consequently you may care for them and honor them, and enjoy through all this a peace and joy that never cease.

4.5.0.en: Then he began to charge him with specific matters, the first of which is almsgiving. If he loves God and is satisfied with His care, he will not accept sin, because it is a breaking of the commandment of God, whom he loves with all his heart. Thus he can give up his selfishness and his anxiety about himself, and love others and care for them and give them the utmost he can of his money and effort.

4.6.0.en: Then he declared to him clearly that he should be merciful and not neglect the poor, lest God neglect him and not hear his petition.

4.7.0.en: He asked him to give according to what he has: if he is rich, to give much, and if he is poor, to give little, but willingly, not attached to money or anxious about his needs.

4.8.0.en: Then he promises him the blessings of almsgiving, for it has a great reward with God. Because of almsgiving God has mercy on him and keeps him far from sin, so that he does not fall into it, and forgives him if he falls, and directs his heart to repentance, and rescues him from death and eternal perdition. Almsgiving gives a firm hope in blessed eternity.

4.8.1.en: It is noted here that when the aged Tobit lost his sight, his inner sight flourished and grew strong within him, so that he was able, with the guidance of the Holy Spirit, to give all these commandments to his son. The son was seeing with his outward eyes, yet he needed the guidance of his father who had lost his sight. Tobit the father speaks with confidence about the importance of almsgiving, which delivers from darkness, that is, eternal torment. This means that he is not troubled by the darkness of his outward eyes, but his heart is attached to the heavenly light in the eternal Kingdom. Therefore he charges his son to care for almsgiving, which brings him to the Kingdom, and not to be occupied, like the rest of men, with material possessions.

4.8.2.en: How great it is to give although what you have is little, even feeling your poverty and material need. For giving is a departure from selfishness and complete trust in the care of God, who blesses the giver with countless blessings. Look at the woman who gave the two mites, and how much the Lord Christ praised her more than all the rich who gave. Giving out of want is the glory of all gifts.

4.9.0.en: Then he warned him against two great sins. The first is the sin of fornication: let him be content with his relationship with his wife, and have no excuse to look at, or think of, or desire another woman, because in this there is covetousness and a treating of sin as permissible. He warned him not to run after any new knowledge of sin in all its corrupt forms.

4.10.0.en: The second sin against which he warned him is the sin of pride, whether in words or even only in thought, because pride is behind all sins and is the chief motive of the sin of fornication. The proud man gives up his carefulness and falls into fornication, whereas God guards the humble from fornication and all sins.

4.11.0.en: Then the father continues with a group of commandments, the first of which is that he pay the hired man his wages at once. This is an application of the commandment of faithfulness and mercy, for the hired man is in need of what he worked for. Therefore delaying the wages is an exploitation of another's money without right, and counts as theft and covetousness.

4.12.0.en: Then he set before him a principle in all his dealings with others: that what he hates for people to do to him, he is not to do to anyone. This verse, and many other verses, were quoted in the New Testament.

4.13.0.en: Then he stresses almsgiving again, but from another understanding: almsgiving is not only to clothe the naked, but also to eat with the poor of what he gives them in alms, in a fellowship of love, whether in a visit to them or on occasions of condolence. It seems that it was common in ancient times, as it is now, to offer alms for the souls of the departed, given to the poor and needy. So he charged him to eat with the poor, but not to mingle with the wicked or eat with them of these foods.

4.14.0.en: He spoke in the spirit of prophecy about the sacrifice of the New Testament, that is, the bread and wine placed on the altar, which is a type of the tomb of the righteous Christ; they become the most holy Body and Blood of the Lord, and all who hunger and thirst after righteousness eat of them, and sinners who do not repent do not eat of them.

4.14.1.en: The Law of the Old Testament forbade approaching or touching tombs, so Tobit here speaks in the spirit of prophecy about the blessing of the bodies of the saints in the New Testament. As for the direct meaning of this verse in the Old Testament, it is the distribution of alms (bread and wine) in the name of the righteous man who died, that the needy may eat of them.

4.15.0.en: Then he asks him for spiritual discipleship at the hands of the wise, that he may hear the counsel of God from their mouths, and then calls him to humility and to seeking the counsel of God in all his affairs, so that he blesses and thanks God, who guides him and cares for him.

4.16.0.en: Finally he gave his son a material charge. Although the father was detached and ascetic, accepting poverty willingly, yet with the tenderness of fatherhood he took pity on his son and wished to provide him with some material comfort. So he charged him to recover the silver that he had lent to Gabael, of which he had a bond (Tob 1:17). In ancient times bonds were written on a piece of skin or clay, and then burned so that the clay would set and become dry and strong. There were two ways of writing bonds:

4.16.1.en: 1- Two identical bonds are written, and the creditor and the debtor each take a copy of it.

4.16.2.en: 2- One bond is written and divided into two halves, and the creditor and the debtor each take a part of the bond. This is what happened in the book of Tobit according to the longer text in the fifth chapter.

4.16.3.en: Bonds are mentioned in the Old Testament with Jeremiah (Jer 32:9-14) and in the New Testament in the parable of the unjust steward (Lk 16).

4.17.0.en: Then he reassured his son that the children of God, although they live in poverty, have good awaiting them in eternity, on condition that they avoid sin and care to do good.

4.17.1.en: The meeting with the angel and his journey with the younger Tobias
